transcript:
Live from NPR News in Washington, I'm Lynda Kenyon.
Chinese leader Xi Jinping says he agreed with President Trump
to set up discussions on AI risks by November.
NPR's Jennifer Pack reports from Beijing.
China says progress has been made in identifying which items
to lower tariffs on, worth $30 billion of goods
in each direction without giving details,
while the White House lists U.S. fish, wood products,
cosmetics and Chinese toys, holiday decorations
and small appliances as items to see tariff reductions.
The White House also says China agreed to buy more American coal
and that Beijing will address U.S. concerns
on rare earth supply shortages.
No mention of these in China's statement.
Both Beijing and Washington say Trump and Xi agreed on Iran
that it should never hold a nuclear weapon
and that no country should charge transit fees
on international waterways.
Jennifer Pack, NPR News, Beijing.
Former Kennedy Center employees say several months ago,
the institution's leadership canceled a plan
to repair significant leaks in the main building.
The center's board now says those leaks were so urgent
that the complex had to close immediately.
NPR's Anastasia Sulkis has more.
In a letter sent to two congressional committees,
the whistleblowers say the center's current executive
director, Matt Floga, had secured $9.3 million
to replace and repair water leaks
in the center's roof and soffits.
Those repairs were approved in August 2025,
according to supplemental documents
also filed with Congress.
But this April, the whistleblowers say
Floga canceled the repair plan
four months before the Kennedy Center's board
approved shutting the arts complex immediately.
They also say some of the waterproofing funds
were diverted for repainting exterior columns
and other cosmetic changes President Trump desired.
The Kennedy Center did not respond immediately
to NPR's request for comment.
Anastasia Sulkis, NPR News.
-A neuro-easter is bearing down on New York
with officials saying the worst is yet to come.
Jessica Gould from member station WNYC has the story.
-Governor Kathy Hochul has called for a state of emergency
in New York City and surrounding areas,
urging people to stay home.
She says not to underestimate the storm
following a calm stretch Saturday afternoon.
-Don't take this lightly.
Don't tempt mother nature.
Don't risk your life.
-The rain is expected to intensify overnight
and through Sunday morning,
with gusty winds and coastal flooding.
And officials say a full moon could worsen flooding.
Already, a few residents in coastal Queens
were kayaking through the streets.
And videos show cars entirely underwater
around a hotel in nearby Edgewater, New Jersey.
Officials are encouraging New Yorkers
to avoid all travel through late Sunday morning.
For NPR News, I'm Jessica Gould in New York.
-You're listening to NPR News.
Alabama has reached a settlement with TikTok.
As NPR's John Ruich reports,
the lawsuit accused the social media company
of designing its platform to be addictive to kids
and then misled consumers about it.
-TikTok has agreed to pay Alabama $100 million,
and that figure could go up to $300 million
if certain conditions are met.
A statement from Alabama's attorney general
says the short video platform also agreed
to implement a series of safety features
designed to protect children.
Those include a two-hour daily time limit
extendable by parents,
pauses that interrupt teens using the platform continuously,
restrictions on nighttime access,
and a prohibition on cosmetic filters for teen users.
The TikTok agreement follows a similar settlement last month
between the social media giant Meta and a group of states.
That case also hinged on whether the social media platforms
were designed to hook kids
and whether the company was truthful to the public about it.
John Ruich, NPR News.
-Communities worldwide dedicated yesterday, 9/25,
as Dolly Parton Day.
The date was a nod to Dolly Parton's hit song "9 to 5."
Many states established the 25th to celebrate Parton's career
as a singer-songwriter, actor, philanthropist,
and an entrepreneur, as well as her commitment
to increasing literacy.
Fans donated to Parton's Imagination Library
while others celebrated by dressing up as the superstar
and toasting with pink-themed cocktails.
Parton died last month after a short battle with cancer.
She was 80 years old.
I'm Linda Kenyon, NPR News, in Washington.

topics.text: Chinese leader Xi Jinping agrees with President Trump to set up discussions on AI risks by November
China and U.S. make progress on tariff reductions and trade agreements following Trump-Xi discussions
Kennedy Center employees say leadership canceled urgent roof leak repairs, diverted funds for cosmetic changes
Nor'easter bearing down on New York with state of emergency declared, worst weather expected overnight
Alabama reaches $100 million settlement with TikTok over addictive platform design targeting children
Communities worldwide celebrate Dolly Parton Day on September 25, honoring late singer's career and philanthropy
